The city library has opened a new reading room for children after a six month renovation. The room opens on Monday and offers free weekend workshops.

A volunteer-run ferry service will restart on Saturday after repairs to the main pier. The first crossing leaves at nine in the morning and additional crossings will run throughout the afternoon. Tickets can be bought at the harbor office. The pier was damaged during a winter storm and has been closed since February.

A research team at a university has tested whether planting trees near bus stops can lower summertime temperatures for passengers. During the experiment, the researchers measured afternoon conditions at forty stops across three neighborhoods. They found that stops next to mature trees were cooler than stops with a metal roof alone. In the hottest part of the day, shade also allowed the ground beneath the trees to retain more moisture. The city plans to use the findings to choose sites for a trial planting program. Officials say the first sites will be selected after residents have had a chance to comment. The program will focus on streets used by people travelling to schools and clinics, where benches and sheltered waiting areas are sparse. Researchers will measure air temperature again after the trees grow and compare it with readings from nearby streets without new trees.
